correctness.rationale: Exact monomial parametrization gives u_jv_j=xyw_j on W_i. Disjoint-leading-monomial Gröbner basis and xy-localization prove primeness and correct scheme-theoretic chart dimension. The character lattice basis and inequalities alpha,beta,gamma,delta >= 0, gamma_j+delta_j >= alpha+beta are explicit. Every extreme ray is enumerated by its two families plus coordinate rays, with no missing options; a unimodular minor proves torsionfreedom and the class group rank. The Jacobian at toric divisors and complete-intersection Serre conditions prove normality. Independent initial quadrics u_jv_j give the squarefree tangent cone and exact multiplicity. The general proof is not a finite experiment.

originality.rationale: The asserted new content is the complete base-edge projective chart description, the explicit 2^(m-1)-component reduced tangent cone, and the exact local class group rank 2^m-2. Ohsugi--Hibi 1999 treats graph toric ideals and pairs of odd cycles sharing a vertex, but not the projective fixed-point local divisor-class group. Higashitani--Matsushita 2021 gives a general global homogeneous edge-ring class-group theorem and torsionfreeness, not these local chart computations or exponential formula. Searches by graph aliases, binomial equations, local invariant formulas, and singularity parameters found no exact published equivalent; this remains evidence-limited, not a uniqueness guarantee.
residual_risks: An unindexed or otherwise unlocated publication may already compute these friendship-graph local toric cones or their class groups.
A broad toric facet-class-group formula may make this a corollary for a reader who already knows the relevant local cone; the explicit cone/ray enumeration remains the asserted new content.

value.rationale: The friendship graph is a canonical connected cactus family for toric edge rings. Determining local Q-factoriality and tangent-cone complexity at natural base-edge fixed points probes intrinsic singular geometry; exact exponential free class ranks and exponentially reducible tangent cones within normal Gorenstein complete intersections are structural, not arbitrary small-number gains. These pointwise invariants are not already supplied by a homogeneous edge-ring class-group theorem. The assertion is bounded to the natural fixed-point orbit and does not claim a global census.
